score.name: Annaly Capital Management, Inc.
score.moat_justification: Weak: scale ($135.6B assets, largest U.S. mortgage REIT), deep repo/swap market access and a diversified three-engine platform (Agency MBS, Residential Credit, MSR) are real but replicable advantages — the assets are commodity securities anyone with financing can buy, spreads are set by the market, and there is no pricing power. Measured returns confirm no durable franchise: fundamentals.json roic_proxy is null for every year (no operating-income tag is filed) and gross margin is null (no revenue tag), while ROE swung from -14.6% (2023) to +7.9% (2024) to +12.6% (2025) — rate/spread-driven, not franchise-driven.

analysis_md:
# NLY — Annaly Capital Management, Inc.

Engine 5.4.0 pass-1 run, 2026-10-17. Price $18.23 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $11,686,209,168 (dcf_numbers.json) — in scope under $40B. **Sector model misfit (Real Estate / mortgage REIT): confidence low throughout, and the method range — not any single tier — is the real headline.**

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed. Filing figures quoted for the balance sheet and the overrides are from the FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-02-12) as cited.

## What it is
The largest U.S. mortgage REIT: an internally managed, REIT-elected capital manager that borrows short (repo and other secured financing) and owns long mortgage assets across three groups — Annaly Agency Group (Agency MBS, $92.9B of the $104.7B portfolio at YE2025), Annaly Residential Credit Group (non-Agency whole loans and securitized products), and Annaly Mortgage Servicing Rights Group (MSR; long-term subservicing/MSR purchase agreement with PennyMac entered October 2025). The economics are a levered spread: asset yield minus funding and hedging cost, at GAAP leverage 7.2:1 / economic leverage 5.6:1 at YE2025 (10-K). Q2 2026 (latest quarter): earnings available for distribution (EAD) $0.79/share vs a raised $0.75 quarterly dividend, book value $20.15/share, economic return 5.5% for the quarter (company Q2 2026 release, via search).

## Owner's earnings
Owner's earnings here = operating cash flow − capex − SBC (conservative definition). The maintenance definition is not computable for the recent years — financials_history.csv carries no D&A figure for 2023–2025, so oe_maintenance is blank there; only the conservative series is used.

- **FY2025:** OCF $692,911,000; capex $0 (override, below); SBC $28,000,000 (override, below) → **conservative OE $664,911,000 = $1.04/share** (base_oe_latest_per_share 1.0372).
- **History (financials_history.csv, post-override):** OE/share 2021 $8.54, 2022 $12.98, 2023 $4.73, 2024 $6.28, 2025 $1.04 — positive 5 of the last 5 years (dcf_numbers.json), but the series is dominated by flows that are not distributable earnings: U.S. Treasury trading settlements and derivative settlements run through OCF, and noncash mark-to-market losses are added back (see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE below).
- **Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct):**
  - OCF: FY $692,911,000 − prior YTD $24,474,000 + current YTD $218,010,000 = **TTM $886,447,000**
  - Capex: **TTM $0** — all three legs filled by the capex override (ttm.json overrides_used)
  - SBC: **TTM $28,000,000** — all three legs filled by the SBC override (YTD legs prorated $13,884,931.51 each way and cancel)
  - Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **732,317,721**
  - **TTM OE total $858,447,000 → base OE/share $1.17** (base_source: ttm_json)
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is **$4.73/share** — rejected as the base; see BASE_DIVERGENCE. The latest-FY base is $1.04/share, close to the TTM base, which corroborates the TTM end of the range.

## OVERRIDES — capex and SBC (the preliminary run exited 4, DATA_GAP)
- **The gap:** the preliminary engine run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP: sbc, capex` — no tier emitted. EDGAR companyfacts carries no annual ShareBasedCompensation fact for 2023–2025 (the tag was last filed for FY2009) and no PPE-capex fact in any year.
- **Capex — $0, kind "filing":** judgment.json carries `capex_override` sourced to the FY2025 10-K Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (p. F-6): the investing section lists only securities, loans, MSR, reverse-repo and JV flows for FY2025/2024/2023 — no PPE purchase line in any year — and the statement reconciles exactly without one (FY2025: 692,911 − 27,362,734 + 27,219,634 = the reported 549,811 net increase in cash, $ thousands; FY2024 and FY2023 reconcile exactly the same way; full arithmetic in judgment.json). The balance sheet carries no property-and-equipment line (ppe_net blank in every history year). Measured impact is nil — the engine history already carried capex as assumed-zero; the override converts a silent zero-fill into a sourced, registered decision. override_checks flags it out_of_band with last_filed_value null (no filed capex value exists to anchor a band); judgment.json carries the ack_reason for that mechanical flag.
- **SBC — $28,000,000, kind "filing":** judgment.json carries `sbc_override` sourced to Note 14 (Long-Term Stock Incentive Plan, p. F-30) of the FY2025 10-K: equity-based compensation expense recognized was $28.0M for FY2025; the same note reports $23.2M (FY2024 10-K) and $17.3M (FY2023 10-K). One override value fills every untagged year, so FY2025's $28.0M is applied to 2023 and 2024 as well — it overstates those years, i.e. errs conservative (more SBC = lower OE), and is immaterial either way (~$0.04/share). override_checks: last_filed_value −$4,514,000 (the stale FY2009 tag), out_of_band false.
- **Measured impact (key_numbers.md, on the TTM base actually used; same final configuration, overrides toggled off):** base OE/share $1.21 (no override) → $1.17 (with override), −3.16%; weighted IRR 8.49% → 8.30% (−0.19pp). Unblocks tier: YES — without the overrides the filing gap blocks scoring entirely. (dcf_numbers.json's separate override_impact block, run on the engine-native normalized base, records the zero-fill baseline at $4.79/share and 26.67% weighted IRR — that is the rejected median base of BASE_DIVERGENCE, shown there only as the both-ways comparison.)

## Moat: 3/10 — weak
Justification (judgment.json): scale ($135.6B assets, largest U.S. mortgage REIT), deep repo/swap market access and a diversified three-engine platform are real but replicable — the assets are commodity securities anyone with financing can buy, spreads are market-set, and there is no pricing power.
- FOR: scale and liquidity ($9.4B of total assets available for financing at YE2025, including $6.1B cash and unencumbered Agency MBS, per the 10-K MD&A); diversified Agency / Residential Credit / MSR platform whose engines partly offset each other across rate cycles (MSR values rise when Agency MBS falls); internally managed, no external-manager fee drag; 25+ years through multiple rate cycles.
- AGAINST: no pricing power — Agency spreads and repo costs are set by the market; structural leverage (GAAP 7.2:1, economic 5.6:1 at YE2025) makes book value hostage to rate/spread moves; persistent ATM dilution (share count +15.9%/yr in the engine history; diluted weighted count 494,541,323 in FY2023 → 641,042,741 in FY2025 → 732,317,721 current-YTD in ttm.json); dividend cut in 2023 and 5-yr DPS CAGR −5.1% (fundamentals.json).
- **ROIC evidence (required check):** fundamentals.json reports roic_proxy as null for every year (Annaly files no operating-income tag) and gross margin as null (no revenue tag) — the standardized ROIC/margin series does not exist for this filer. The return series that does exist is ROE: −14.6% (2023), +7.9% (2024), +12.6% (2025) (fundamentals.json annual) — sign-flipping and rate-driven, i.e. no demonstrated through-cycle return above the cost of capital. That is why the moat is 3 and cannot be argued higher on this evidence.
- A 3 gives CAP = 5.9 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 5.9 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-17)
**Growth recalibration (written reason):** the engine's blended growth is −53.15%, a single component (OE/share CAGR 2y −53.15%) built from two OCF artifacts — FY2023 OE/share $4.73 in a year GAAP net income was −$1,643,171,000 (OCF propped by noncash addbacks) and FY2025 OE/share $1.04 in a year OCF absorbed $1,822,026 thousand of net payments on derivatives (10-K cash-flow statement). The engine floors g_base at −5.0%. The company's actual distributable prints are not collapsing: FY2025 EAD was $2.92/share and Q1/Q2 2026 printed $0.76/$0.79 with the dividend raised from $0.70 to $0.75 (company releases, via search). Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets (−0.13 / −0.03 / +0.05 / +0.10 / +0.15 vs g_base) to −10 / −8 / **0** / +5 / +10% — centered flat on the TTM base, with the bear end carrying the rate-shock case. Probabilities 15/30/25/20/10 (bear weight widened per OE_VOLATILE, defaults 10/25/30/25/10); OE multipliers at the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $18.23.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −10.0% | 0.75 | Rate/spread shock: funding costs jump, book value and EAD fall, dividend cut again (2022–23 pattern) | $4.60 | 5.39% |
| Bear | 30% | −8.0% | 0.90 | Spreads stay wide, hedge costs stay heavy; TTM-level OE decays | $5.94 | 6.32% |
| Base | 25% | 0.0% | 1.00 | TTM OE/share $1.17 holds, then fades to terminal over the 5.9-yr CAP | $8.80 | 8.48% |
| Bull | 20% | +5.0% | 1.10 | EAD momentum (Q2 2026 $0.79) rebuilds cash earnings toward the dividend | $11.54 | 10.46% |
| Super bull | 10% | +10.0% | 1.25 | Steep curve + tight spreads: carry compounds, book value grows | $15.56 | 13.24% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $8.54 (−53.2% vs price), IV@12% $11.19, IV@10% $14.14, weighted IRR 8.30%, base-case IRR 8.48%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Bear tier D (6.32%), bull tier C (10.46%) — see TIER_BAND. Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 6.43%, terminal value 17.5% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.38x, 9.5 months since FY end. Hurdle-clearing prices: clears 15% only at or below $8.54, 20% at $6.13, 25% at $4.79 (hurdle_prices).

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:sbc / DATA_GAP:capex** (preliminary run): resolved by the two filing-sourced overrides above; data_gap_uncovered is empty in the final run.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:sbc / OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex**: see OVERRIDES — gap, sources, band/ack status, and measured impact are recorded in judgment.json, dcf_numbers.json (overrides_applied, override_checks, override_impact) and the central registry, not just here.
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 9.5 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted above.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY $1.04 vs 3-yr median $4.73): **the median is the distorted one.** Its median year is FY2023, when OCF of $2,367,203,000 was reported alongside GAAP net income of −$1,643,171,000: the 10-K cash-flow statement bridges the gap with $3,310,579 thousand of net (gains) losses on investments and derivatives added back — noncash mark-to-market losses treated as if they were not economic costs — plus $2,015,608 thousand of proceeds from U.S. Treasury securities. Book value fell and the dividend was cut that year; that OCF is not distributable earnings power. The latest/TTM end is depressed by real hedge-settlement cash costs ($1,822,026 thousand of net payments on derivatives in FY2025), which are a genuine cost of the levered carry. TTM base used; the median is retained above and in the method range, not hidden.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (>40% in 2023, 2024, 2025): same mechanism, all three years — for a mortgage REIT the NI↔OCF gap is structural, not a one-off: FY2025 net income $2,027,262,000 vs OCF $692,911,000 (derivative settlement payments and premium/discount amortization run through OCF); FY2023 is the mirror image above. This is precisely why the OCF-based OE series is treated as a conservative floor here rather than as earnings power, and why confidence is low.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years: $1.04–$12.98 in the filed history): real and structural (see above). Handled by the TTM base, bear-heavy probabilities (45% on bear-or-worse), and sizing the verdict to the conservative end.
- **DILUTION** (share count +15.9%/yr): the growth is ATM issuance, not SBC — Annaly raised $2,910,571 thousand of net stock-offering proceeds in FY2025 (10-K cash-flow statement) and the FY2025 10-K reports 706,972,452 shares issued and outstanding at YE2025 vs a 641,042,741 weighted diluted count; fundamentals.json shows TTM share issuance of $2,609,634,000 against dividends paid of $1,569,015,000. SBC itself is small and roughly flat ($17.3M → $23.2M → $28.0M disclosed, FY2023–25). The dilution is partly accretive by design (issuance above book adds book value/share) but it means per-share OE must outrun a rapidly growing count — one more reason the TTM share count (732,317,721) is the right denominator.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK** (no debt tag for the latest FY — net debt unknown, not zero): stated from the filing. FY2025 Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition (10-K, $ thousands): total assets $135,609,838; total liabilities $119,449,927, comprising repurchase agreements $81,865,723, debt issued by securitization vehicles $28,918,753, U.S. Treasury securities sold, not yet purchased $2,396,724, participations issued $1,932,655, other secured financing $1,075,000, plus payables/interest/dividends payable; total GAAP debt $116,188,855 per the leverage reconciliation; stockholders' equity $16,090,772 (dcf_numbers history). GAAP leverage 7.2:1, economic leverage 5.6:1. The engine's debt tags capture almost none of this (repo/securitization debt is not filed under its debt tags), so net_debt_latest is null and no net-debt ratio is quoted — leverage verdict: this is a 7x-levered balance sheet by the filer's own ratio, full stop.
- **CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED**: confirmed and quantified from the filing — the FY2025 cash figure $2,037,838 thousand includes $1,683,059 thousand of cash pledged as collateral (10-K balance-sheet parenthetical); the encumbered/unencumbered table leaves only $354,779 thousand unencumbered. Any net-debt figure built on the headline cash would be understated by the pledged amount; another reason no net-debt number is quoted.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Real Estate): accepted — an OCF/capex DCF fits a levered mortgage REIT poorly (OCF contains trading and hedge-settlement flows; the market prices this name on EAD and book value, $20.15/share at Q2 2026 vs the $18.23 price). Confidence is low and the name belongs with the sector misfits in the ranking.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear D 6.32% vs bull C 10.46%): the verdict is sized to the bear end — Tier D stands; even the super-bull case (13.24%) does not clear 15% on the scored base.

## My thoughts / method range
- **The method range is the finding.** Same scenario ladder, three defensible bases (all measured with this run's engine, --measure probes): TTM OE $1.17/share → **Tier D, weighted IRR 8.30%, IV@15% $8.54** (scored); the company's own EAD $2.92/share (FY2025, company release) → Tier B, weighted IRR 17.12%, IV@15% $21.26; the engine's 3-yr median OCF base $4.73/share → Tier S, weighted IRR 26.38%. A Tier S print for a 7x-levered mREIT whose median OCF year was a −$1.64B GAAP loss year would be a fake — the median is rejected for the reason documented under BASE_DIVERGENCE, and the scored result is the conservative (TTM) end.
- What the market is actually paying for at $18.23: 0.90x Q2 2026 book value ($20.15) and a $0.75 quarterly dividend that EAD covered for the ninth consecutive quarter in Q2 2026 ($0.79 vs $0.75). On EAD the name is roughly fairly priced to modestly cheap (Tier B probe); on filing-direct cash OE it is expensive. Neither supports a 15%+ expected return with any margin — the dividend is the return, and it was cut as recently as 2023.
- Risks: rate/spread shock against 7.2x GAAP leverage; repo funding is short-dated and confidence-sensitive; continued ATM dilution if the price holds above book; preferred stack ahead of the common (Series I redeemed October 2026 per company news, via search — capital mix still carries multiple preferred series).
- Data notes: enrichment (fundamentals, prices, segments, statements, profile/street, reprice) all ran clean after scoring — segments.json carries the three segment groups (net income, assets, net interest income by Agency / Residential Credit / MSR); live.json repricing at the same $18.23 close leaves the tier unchanged (delta 0.0pp).

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 8.30% on the TTM base; method range D to S across defensible bases, EAD-implied B — the range itself is the finding)
- Confidence: **Low** (sector model mismatch, OCF-based OE is a floor not earnings power for an mREIT, 3.38x scenario spread)
- One-liner: Diversified mortgage REIT with scale but no pricing power, moat 3/10 — on filing-direct TTM owner's earnings ($1.17/share) it cannot clear the 15% hurdle at $18.23 (weighted IRR 8.3%, weighted IV@15% $8.54; clears 15% only below ~$8.54); the 3-yr median base prints a fake Tier S off noncash mark-to-market addbacks and the company's own EAD ($2.92/share FY2025) reaches only Tier B — sector model misfit, confidence low.
